meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Mark Dawson (CISO - Lighthouse Retail); Priya Martinez (Head of Cloud); Liam O'Reilly (Compliance Manager)
Recording: Yes
Notes: Trust center and control mapping requested; customer evaluating Dedicated vs Private for BYOK.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Mark: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:07] Jordan: Cool, quick agenda - SOC2/ISO posture, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and encryption/KMS questions. Priya from SE will cover technical bits.
[00:18] Priya (SE): hi all, thanks. I'll jump into the infra details after we recap what Lighthouse already has in scope.
[00:25] Mark: For context, Lighthouse is preparing for our own annual SOC 2 audit in Q2 and want to make sure vendors align. We're evaluating Redwood for inference and want to validate both hosted and dedicated models. Key asks: 1) get your SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs, 2) map your controls to our control matrix, 3) understand audit log access + retention, 4) KMS options (BYOK?), and 5) SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[00:48] Priya S: got it. Jordan, you can share the SOC2 artifacts; from SE side I'll cover the logging and KMS nuance between hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
[00:55] Jordan: quick note, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs documented in our Trust Center. I'll send the link and a downloadable package.
[01:02] Liam: are the reports redacted or full? We need evidence of control implementation for certain areas.
[01:06] Jordan: usually we provide the full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; the trust center has executive summaries and an option to request full reports. We'll mark the NDA step.
[01:14] Mark: ok. For controls mapping - we have an ISO27001 matrix and need Redwood's mapping to specific controls (A.8, A.10 etc) and SOC2 CC criteria.
[01:22] Priya S: we maintain a controls mapping template; I'll populate Redwood controls and map them to ISO and SOC criteria. I'll also include evidence artifacts (e.g., policy docs, screenshots, sample logs) where permissible.
[01:31] Mark: great. On audit logs - we want immutable logs with at least 1 year retention and ability to export on request. How does Redwood handle access to audit logs for hosted tenants?
[01:41] Priya S: for hosted we keep tenant-level audit logs - API access is available via the trust center for partners; for customers we can provide extracts and long-term retention as an add-on. There's a standard 90-day retention for the hosted default but you can purchase extended retention or use Dedicated/Private for longer retention guarantees.
[01:54] Mark: hmm that's a flag - we prefer 12 months included. Is extended retention expensive?
[01:58] Jordan: pricing is configurable; we'll include pricing details. For Dedicated or Private, retention policies are customer-configurable and we can meet 12 months out of the box.
[02:07] Liam: for audit purposes, do logs include user identity (SSO principal), API keys, and request/response metadata? Also are logs tamper-evident?
[02:16] Priya S: yes - logs capture the auth principal, route, timestamps, IP, and token metadata; we can produce signed log hashes for tamper-evidence on request or via a SIEM integration.
[02:26] Mark: good. Next, SSO and RBAC - we use Okta and want SCIM provisioning, SAML-based SSO, and role-based access controls that map to our internal roles. Can Redwood support SCIM?
[02:36] Jordan: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts. Roles in the console map to RBAC policies; Priya can share the RBAC matrix and API for enforcement.
[02:44] Priya S: specifically, you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and enforce least-privilege on routes (e.g., read-only audit vs admin). We also support session timeout and MFA enforcement via SAML.
[02:55] Priya M (cust): any limitations on automated provisioning for Dedicated clusters?
[02:59] Priya S: no major limitations - SCIM works with Dedicated. For Private on-prem we may need SCIM endpoint connectivity; we usually run a lightweight connector if firewall rules block direct provisioning.
[03:11] Mark: KMS - our security team requires customer-managed keys for encryption at rest for production models. Do you support BYOK / customer KMS integration?
[03:19] Priya S: yes. For Private deployments you can fully manage keys in your KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer integration with customer KMS for key wrapping; for hosted we have an option for customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS integration but not all regions support BYOK today. We'll detail region support in the controls doc.
[03:35] Mark: what about key rotation and key separation for different tenants?
[03:39] Priya S: we support rotation via customer KMS policies; per-tenant key separation is available on Dedicated and Private; on hosted we can do envelope encryption with per-tenant key wrapping where supported.
[03:48] Liam: evidence - can you produce KMS access logs and encryption key use logs for audits?
[03:53] Priya S: yes we can export key usage logs and integrate with customer SIEM or provide extracts. For Private you'll have direct access to KMS logs in your environment.
[03:59] Jordan: I'll flag that in the controls mapping; we'll include sample key usage logs.
[04:04] Mark: data residency is also important - we need EU-only processing for some workloads. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
[04:11] Priya S: yes, requests can be routed to region-specific clusters; for EU-only processing we recommend Dedicated EU clusters or Private deployment in your VPC to guarantee residency. Hosted can be configured for region preference but has some cross-region fallback options which you can opt out of.
[04:26] Mark: ok, we'll likely push for Dedicated EU. Anything else on data residency?
[04:30] Priya S: we'll document network egress paths and data flows in the mapping packet.
[04:34] Mark: auditing: do you have SOC 2 controls around change management, infra hardening, vulnerability scanning? We need specifics for auditors.
[04:41] Jordan: yes - our SOC2 includes change control, code reviews, patching cadence, vuln scanning results. Priya, we'll attach the relevant policies and sample scans.
[04:49] Priya S: we also run automated infra scanning and a scheduled pentest program; pen test summary can be shared as part of the trust center under NDA.
[04:57] Liam: network segmentation - for Dedicated, can we have private networking and restrict outbound access?
[05:02] Priya S: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private subnets. For Private you have full control. For hosted there are egress controls and allow/deny lists.
[05:09] Mark: compliance artifacts - will you provide an artifacts pack we can feed into our auditors?
[05:14] Jordan: yes, we'll assemble an artifacts pack: SOC2 report, ISO cert, control mapping, sample policies, and log extracts where allowed.
[05:20] Mark: timing - we need the pack within a week.
[05:22] Jordan: I'll aim for 48-72 hours on the initial package; full controls mapping will take until end of week.
[05:29] Priya M: a couple technical clarifications - when you say audit log exports are available, what's the format and delivery mechanism?
[05:36] Priya S: exports are JSON/CSV and we can push to an S3 bucket or provide a signed download. SIEM integrations via syslog or API are supported for Dedicated and Private.
[05:45] Mark: for tamper evidence, you mentioned signed log hashes - can you elaborate?
[05:49] Priya S: we create periodic hashes of log batches and sign them with our signing key; for Dedicated/Private we can plumb those into customer KMS or provide an HMAC you control. We'll note options in the doc.
[06:01] Mark: auditor question - do you have third-party attestations beyond SOC2/ISO (e.g., penetration test vendor reports)?
[06:07] Jordan: we have annual third-party pentests; summaries are in the trust center and full reports available under NDA.
[06:12] Liam: any specific limitations we should document? For example, are there any endpoints that store PII in logs by default?
[06:19] Priya S: we scrub sensitive PII from logs by default; request/response bodies are not logged unless enabled for debug and then masked. We'll include our logging policy and masking rules.
[06:29] Mark: encryption in transit - TLS versions supported?
[06:32] Priya S: TLS 1.2+ is enforced; we recommend 1.3 where supported. Mutual TLS is available for private peering.
[06:39] Jordan: quick note on tooling - Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency but also audit trails for API keys and admin actions.
[06:46] Mark: good. We also need a sample incident response playbook and breach notification timelines for our contract.
[06:52] Jordan: we provide an incident response summary and SLA for notification times; we'll include it in the artifacts pack.
[06:58] Liam: regarding RBAC mapping - can Redwood provide a CSV export of role assignments for our auditors?
[07:03] Priya S: yes, role assignments can be exported and we can include a sample audit export.
[07:07] Mark: any questions from your side?
[07:10] Priya M: one small ask - can we get a sample of the controls mapping format so we can pre-fill our questions?
[07:16] Jordan: will attach a template with the initial packet.
[07:20] Mark: perfect. It sounds like deliverables are: SOC2/ISO certs, control mapping, sample logs, RBAC export, KMS usage logs, and pricing for retention.
[07:29] Jordan: yes. We'll also surface any region limitations for BYOK and confirm SLAs for retention.
[07:36] Mark: timeline recap?
[07:38] Jordan: initial artifacts in 48-72 hours, controls mapping by 2026-11-30, technical deep-dive week of 2026-12-07.
[07:47] Liam: sounds good.
[07:49] Priya S: one last note - for pilot workloads we recommend Dedicated EU to meet residency and retention without custom contracts.
[07:58] Mark: we'll discuss internally but that aligns.
[08:01] Jordan: thanks everyone - action items in the invite; we'll follow up.
[08:05] Mark: thanks Jordan, bye.
[58:00] [call end]

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings present, speaker labels occasionally consolidated. Some proper nouns (Redwood product names, KV cache) may be transcribed differently in places.
